recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No further core FHIR source work is needed for FHIR-11056; future changes to security-label matching or value-set scope should be handled under later, specific Jira decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-11056 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core Consent. It asked to replace the DSTU2 Consent.except.securityLabel definition, 'A set of security labels that define which resources are controlled by this exception. If more than one label is specified, all resources must have all the specified labels,' with 'A security label, comprised of 0..* security label fields (Privacy tags), which define which resources are controlled by this exception.'
initial_application: Historical commit 0f594b3938a50781639ecd7fa5930288595d9bfe explicitly applied CR 11055 and CR 11056 by changing the old Consent spreadsheet source from the rejected set-of-labels wording to the approved singular security-label definition. Later source refactors carried that wording into the current Consent StructureDefinition as Consent.provision.securityLabel.
additional_context: Consent is active in source/fhir.ini, and source/consent/structuredefinition-Consent.xml is the current authoritative StructureDefinition input. The former DSTU2 Consent.except.securityLabel element is now represented as Consent.provision.securityLabel. Related FHIR-11055 explains the adjacent purpose-of-use comment, FHIR-10707 records that no narrower security-label value set was adopted, and the already-published FHIR-36354 reconciliation refined the hierarchical-label comment without changing the FHIR-11056 definition.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already contains the approved FHIR-11056 definition, and searches did not find a current Consent provision/exception definition still using the rejected 'set of security labels' wording.

related_jiras.note: Applied in the same historical commit and explains the purpose-of-use sentence that remains in the Consent.provision.securityLabel comment.
Resolved no-change issue about whether to narrow security-label values, supporting that FHIR-11056 did not require a value-set change.
Later Published Consent issue refined the hierarchical-label comment without changing the FHIR-11056 definition.
